title: fix(service-job): a run row records the trigger of the call that ran it, and a replay is one row
body:
Fixes #32406

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：`DbJobAdapter` 写 `sys_job_run` 行时，`trigger` 列按这一次调用来定：定时触发写 `schedule`，手动 `trigger()` 写 `manual`，`replay()` 只写一行 `replay`（每次尝试一行，重试时每行都是 `replay`）。
- 为什么改：以前这个值在注册 job 时就写死成 `schedule`，手动运行在运行历史里看起来像定时运行，一次重放会留下两行（一行 `replay`、一行 `schedule`），运维看不出哪次是手动的，重放也被算成两次。
- 风险与回滚：只改运行历史的记录值和重放的行数，job 本身的执行、重试、超时、`sys_job` 汇总计数都不变；处理函数收到的上下文不变（重放仍告诉处理函数 `manual`）。代码里没有读 `sys_job_run.trigger` 的消费者。回滚即还原本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/services/service-job/src/db-job-adapter.ts` 的 `runTriggerOf` 与 `replay()` 末尾（重放如何把 `replay` 标记交给它将要运行的那个包装函数），以及 `wrap()` 上新增的取值表。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-job exec vitest run src/db-job-adapter.test.ts -t "records the trigger of the call"`，预期 10 个全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`DbJobAdapter.wrap()` used to take the run row's `trigger` as an argument fixed at `schedule()` time (`'schedule'`), and the same wrapper serves every way a job runs: the elected scheduler's fire, and `inner`'s `trigger()` / `replay()` (on the no-cron fallback `inner` owns the timer too). So every row said `schedule`, and `replay()` wrote its own synthetic `replay` row beside the wrapper's `schedule` row.

Now the value is read per invocation, once, before the first attempt (`runTriggerOf`):

| The call | `sys_job_run.trigger` |
|:---|:---|
| `replay()`'s scope, naming this very wrapper, first invocation | `replay` |
| context says `manual` (`trigger()`, through either timer adapter) | `manual` |
| context says `schedule` (a timer's fire) | `schedule` |
| context says nothing | `schedule` |

The last row is a statement about who can call, not a tolerance: `JobHandler`'s `trigger` is optional by contract, the only caller that may omit it is the injected `cron` adapter (any `IJobService`), and `DbJobAdapter` never calls that adapter's `trigger()`, so a call through it is its scheduled fire. `inner`, which serves every manual call, always states it.

**Replay.** `inner.trigger()` hands the wrapper a context that can only say `manual` (the spec's `JobRunTrigger` is `schedule | manual`, and its TSDoc says a replay runs through `trigger()`; `packages/spec` is untouched). So `replay()` opens an `AsyncLocalStorage` scope (`node:async_hooks`, already used by `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/service-automation`) carrying a one-shot claim that names the exact wrapper `inner` holds for the job. That wrapper's first invocation in the scope takes the tag; anything else the replayed handler starts — another job's `trigger()`, a second call of the same job, a timer armed inside it — finds the claim taken or naming another wrapper and records its own trigger. The wrapper is read after the replay guard's `await`, in the same tick as `inner.trigger()`, so a re-schedule during the guard does not leave the claim naming a stale wrapper. `replay()`'s synthetic `startRun` / `finishRun` and its read-back of `inner.getExecutions()` are gone: the wrapper's own row is the replay's, settled from inside the retry/timeout policy like every other run. `startRun` now has one call site.

The handler's context is unchanged: a replayed handler is told `trigger: 'manual'`, and its `runId` now names the `replay` row (before: the `schedule` row), which is what a sync-in pull records as `job_run_id`.

**Consumers of `sys_job_run.trigger`** (grep at `7d82b2da`, `packages/**`, `ui/**`, `examples/**`, non-test): none read the value. The column is declared in `packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-job-run.object.ts` (`['schedule', 'manual', 'replay']`) and written only by `DbJobAdapter.startRun`. The sync-in path (ADR-0153 D7) reads the handler context's `trigger`, not the row, and is unchanged; `app-artifact-handlers.job-pull-run.test.ts` asserts row count and status on a manual run, not the row trigger. Clause-② stays `no` as the claim declared.

**Docs.** `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx` documents `trigger (schedule | manual | replay)`; that sentence was false for manual and replay runs and is now true, so no doc edit. No sentence was made false.

## Tests

<details><summary>Before (card step 1), new pins on unmodified `origin/main` 7d82b2da code — 7 failed, 2 passed</summary>

```text
trigger() writes manual (both assemblies):
  expected [ 'schedule', 'schedule' ] to deeply equal [ 'manual', 'schedule' ]
replay() writes ONE row (both assemblies), and the handler-context pin:
  expected [ ... ] to have a length of 1 but got 2
retried replay:
  received [replay,1,success] [schedule,1,failed] [schedule,2,success]
  (the synthetic replay row said `success` for attempt 1 while the wrapper's row said `failed`)
replay tag scoping:
  received [job,replay] [job,schedule] [other,schedule] [job,schedule] [other,schedule]
Tests  7 failed | 2 passed | 24 skipped (33)
```

So on a real `DbJobAdapter`: `trigger()` wrote `schedule`; `replay()` wrote 2 rows, `replay` + `schedule`. The scheduled-tick pins passed before and after (that path was already right).
</details>

<details><summary>After, on head c9be4172</summary>

```text
pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-job test        Test Files 12 passed (12) · Tests 155 passed (155)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-job typecheck   tsc --noEmit exit 0 (12 *.test.ts files in the program)
pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-job build       check-dts-emitted: 2/2 declaration files present
```
</details>

New pins (one top-level `describe` in `db-job-adapter.test.ts`): a scheduled tick writes `schedule`, `trigger()` writes `manual`, `replay()` writes ONE `replay` row settled to the run's status — each on both assemblies (with a cron adapter, and without one where `inner` owns the timer and the manual calls through the same wrapper); a replayed handler is told `manual` and the replay row's id; every attempt of a retried replay is `replay`; the tag belongs to the replayed run alone; a re-schedule during the replay guard still replays as `replay`.

Stale pins corrected: `db-job-adapter.test.ts` `recordRuns: true` case (`trigger: 'schedule'` after `trigger('on')` → `manual`), the replay cases in the same file, `db-job-adapter.timeout.test.ts` and `db-job-adapter.degraded-outcome.test.ts` (two rows → one `replay` row).

<details><summary>Ablation (once): the per-call read removed</summary>

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on `db-job-adapter.ts`, anchor `return ctx.trigger ?? 'schedule';` → `return 'schedule';`: anchor 1 → 0, blob `e3dca2049082` → `7352a4aebce4`. `src/db-job-adapter.test.ts`: **4 failed** — `recordRuns: true is the same as the default`, `trigger() writes manual` ×2, the tag-scoping pin. Restored: blob == HEAD (`e3dca2049082`), `git diff HEAD` empty. (Imports are relative `./db-job-adapter.js`, so the run reads source, not `dist/`.)

Reverse check of the race pin: the `db-job-adapter.ts` of `47fbdc67` (wrapper read before the guard's await) put back on disk → `expected [ 'manual' ] to deeply equal [ 'replay' ]`; restored, `git diff HEAD` empty, blob == HEAD.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- `sys_job_run.attempt`'s description (`'1 for first run, >1 for retries/replays'`, `sys-job-run.object.ts`) and `jobs.mdx` ("higher for retries and replays") say a replay's attempt is above 1. No code ever wrote that: the synthetic replay row and the wrapper's row both started at attempt 1, before and after this PR. Pre-existing doc drift, not made false here, outside the file surface (`platform-objects` carries regenerated i18n bundles); noted, not filed.
- Not measured locally: runtime / trigger-schedule suites that run the real `DbJobAdapter` (their dependency closures are not built here; files fail to load, not to assert). Public types and exports are byte-unchanged; CI's Test Core runs them.
